#### 🟠 E-105 — UP & DOWN COULD NOT CONGRATULATE ANYONE, AND IT WAS TWO SILENCES MEETING

Ali's mandate: *"make sure they have the perfect popup on win"*. The reason there was none is
more interesting than the fix, and **neither half was in any tracker**:

**① The board never SENT the data.** `myStakesByMarket` recorded a settled position **only when
`finalPayout === stake`** — a refund. A **WIN and a LOSS were both recorded as nothing**, and
`myUpStake`/`myDownStake` are zeroed the instant a position leaves `OPEN` because *"only live
money counts as you're in"*. ⛔ **So a winner and a loser received byte-identical board props.**
No surface could have congratulated anyone; the data was never sent. (The **round page** was
fine — `getRoundDetail` has carried `myPosition.result` all along, which is why
`YOUR RESULT · PAID OUT` renders there. The asymmetry is the finding.)

**② The celebration existed and could never fire.** `WinCelebrationHost` — a calm gilt popup
with a rolling counter, already built, already mounted once in `AppShell` — is dispatched by
`notify-poller.tsx`, gated on a `readStoredBet()` **localStorage** record that the Up & Down
quick-bet path never writes, and gated behind notifications, which
`perEventNotificationsSuppressed()` turns off for UPDOWN. ⭐ **Suppressing the MESSAGE also
suppressed the MOMENT** — a consequence of the 2026-07-24 decision that nobody had noticed.

**What shipped, and what it deliberately does NOT do.** `BoardRound` gains `myResult`
`{status, side, stake, payout}` from the same positions read (no second query), and a shared
`UpDownResultAnnouncer` mounted on **both** the board and the round page fires on the **observed
prop transition** the `RefreshPoller` delivers. ⛔ **In-app only** — Ali's 2026-07-24 suppression
is untouched, and **§4 of the guard fails if this feature ever grows an email, push or inbox
call**, so it cannot silently reverse an owner decision.

⛔ **Three things it gets right that are easy to get wrong:**
· **It fires on a TRANSITION, never on mount.** A popup that fires because you opened a page is
  an ambush, and it would re-congratulate a player on every visit. The first render only SEEDS.
· **The celebrated figure is `finalPayout`, the REALISED amount.** The existing celebration path
  headlines `stored.payoutIfWin` from **place-time** — its own comment concedes it *"may differ
  slightly from the realised payout"* — and on a pari-mutuel pool it does. A celebrated number
  that is not the number paid is a false money statement on the most screenshot-able screen in
  the product. 📌 **That is still true of the long-form poll path and is left as a separate
  finding, not silently changed here.**
· **A refund is neither a win nor a loss.** The status is read off the **position row**, never
  inferred from the round's outcome, because a round can resolve DOWN and still return an UP
  backer's whole stake when nobody took the other side (E-65). ⚠️ **RG:** the loss is *not* the
  win's mirror — no glow, no counter, no haptic, and it **names the amount**, because a result
  screen that will not name the number is the euphemism the harm rules exist to prevent.

#### 🔴🔴 E-106 — THE TRILINGUAL SWEEP HAS NEVER ONCE MEASURED A TRANSLATION

⛔ **`scripts/live-s29-sweep.mjs` switched language by loading `/api/locale?set=<loc>&next=/`, and
THERE IS NO `/api/locale` ROUTE IN THIS APPLICATION.** The app resolves language from the
**`kp-locale` cookie** (`src/app/layout.tsx:97`, `src/lib/i18n-server.ts:19`). The `goto` was
wrapped in `.catch(() => {})`, so the 404 was swallowed and the run continued.

**Measured, not inferred** (`.qa-s30/probe-locale.mjs`): after `?set=sw`, **`<html lang>` is
`"en"`**, **no locale cookie exists at all**, zero Swahili markers are present and the English
ones all are. Same for `zh`.

⇒ **Every SW and ZH screenshot this campaign has ever captured is English, photographed a second
time.** This session's own fan-out produced **32 player + 104 admin** shots in that state, and
the agents reading them filed things like *"the Chinese admin console is not Chinese"* and
*"Swahili status chips break the pill shape"* — ⛔ **all of it void, and it would have sent the
next session hunting i18n defects that are artefacts of one unroutable URL.** Session 29's
handoff named `player 360 sw,zh` as *the single highest-yield cell in the grid*; it was the one
cell that could not work.

**Fixed two ways, because the first alone would just be a different guess:**
1. the cookie is set directly on the context — `c.addCookies([{ name: "kp-locale", value: locale,
   url: BASE }])`, no endpoint involved;
2. ⭐ **the sweep now REFUSES TO CAPTURE if the locale did not take.** It reads `<html lang>` —
   written from the *same resolved locale the dictionary lookup uses*, so it is the honest
   witness rather than the cookie we just set, which only proves we asked — and **throws** on a
   mismatch. **A sweep that silently captures the wrong language is worse than one that fails,
   because its output looks like evidence.** Verified: `locale sw confirmed (<html lang>="sw")`.

📌 **The same run surfaced three routes in the sweep's own list returning HTTP 404** —
`/history`, `/inbox`, `/kyc` — while the avatar menu links `/profile/kyc`. **Not yet filed**:
that is very likely three wrong paths in the harness rather than three missing pages, and it
needs one minute of checking against the real router before anyone calls it a defect.

⭐ **THE GENERALISABLE LESSON, and it is the third instance today:** *a fetch whose failure is
swallowed by `.catch(() => {})` is a silent assumption.* §3's `pg` trap had a remedy that did not
exist; this had an endpoint that did not exist; the E-64 driver had a selector that matched
something permanent. **Every one produced confident output.** The defence that worked all three
times was the same: *ask the system to tell you the state you just tried to set, and refuse to
proceed if it disagrees.*

#### ✅ E-105 DRIVEN LIVE — a real two-sided round, a real winner, and two defects the drive found

#### 🟠 E-70 — TWO SESSIONS "COULD NOT REPRODUCE" IT BECAUSE THEY DROVE THE WRONG VERB

Ali, 2026-08-06, mid-session: *"urgent fix. when i click **back to app** from admin, it
redirect to app but with no navbar."* **That one word closed it.** `Back to app` is a
`<Link href="/">` in `admin-shell.tsx` — a **client-side soft navigation**. Every previous
attempt reproduced it with `page.goto()`, which is a **hard load**: the server re-renders the
root layout, `x-pathname` is `/`, the chrome appears, and the defect vanishes. **The gesture had
to be a CLICK.** ⛔ *A negative result is only as good as the verb you drove it with.*

**The mechanism is a LAYOUT bug, not the session bug the filing assumed** — and one cause
explains both halves. `AppShell` is a **server component in the ROOT layout** that decides the
player chrome from the **`x-pathname` request header**; in the App Router **a layout is not
re-executed on a soft navigation**, it is preserved. So the shell-less layout rendered for
`/admin` survives the click and the landing page renders inside it. **The mirror is the same
bug:** the avatar menu's `<Link href="/admin">` keeps the *player* layout and renders the
console inside player chrome — **session 21's unexplained *"/admin/updown served the signed-out
player shell to a freshly signed-in ADMIN"*, finally explained.** Ali's *"until I login as a
player or retry the URL"* is simply *any hard load fixes it*.

**Measured on production**, same URL, same session, same account: **click → `nav=0 []`** ·
**hard load → `nav=2 ["Primary","Primary"]`**, and after the click a `Markets` nav link is
**not clickable at all**. ⚠️ **My first detector was junk and I nearly cited it**: a
`position:fixed` bottom-bar probe returned `false` on the CONTROL too, so it could not tell the
two apart — the `nav` landmark count is the honest measure, and the control is what exposed the
detector.

**Fix:** both crossings become plain `<a>`. A full document load is the **correct primitive**
when moving between two entirely different shells, not a de-optimisation — and both call sites
now carry the reasoning, because the change looks like an oversight to anyone who does not know
it. The guard's **§3 control** proves its own parser still sees a legitimate soft `<Link>`
(otherwise §1/§2 would pass over an empty result set), and **§4 is a tripwire**: if someone
later restructures into route groups, it fails and forces a human to re-read E-70 before
deleting the mitigation. 📌 The RED harness carries a **documented-miss** mutation — making §4
always-true cannot fail the suite — recorded honestly rather than hidden.

🔴🔴 **A THIRD NEAR-MISS — AND IT IS NOT A NEW TRAP, IT IS §3's VERY FIRST ONE, RE-PAID. THE
REASON IS THE FINDING: §3's STATED REMEDY DID NOT EXIST.** ⛔ **The `pg` driver's `Date` is
wrong by this machine's UTC offset.**

The settled round page renders its **auditable settlement proof** as
`CLOSE · quoted 00:01:00 EAT · Observed 00:02:29 EAT`. My probe read the same round with
`row.closesAt.toISOString()` and got **`2026-08-05T18:01:00.000Z` = 21:01 EAT**. Three hours
apart, on the **auditable record** — which would be a false statement of exactly the class this
campaign exists to find, and I was one commit away from filing it.

**Measured instead of assumed** (`.qa-s30/probe-time.cjs` prints five representations of one
instant side by side, and names the session timezone rather than assuming it):

| representation | value |
|---|---|
| `current_setting('TIMEZONE')` | **`Etc/UTC`** |
| `"closesAt"::text` | `2026-08-05 21:01:00` ← **no offset suffix ⇒ the column is `timestamp WITHOUT time zone`** |
| `("closesAt" at time zone 'UTC')::text` | `2026-08-05 21:01:00+00` |
| driver `Date` → `.toISOString()` | `2026-08-05T18:01:00.000Z` ← 🔴 **the lie** |
| what the page shows | `00:01:00 EAT` = 21:01 UTC + 3 ✅ **correct** |

⭐ **Prisma maps `DateTime` to `timestamp(3)` WITHOUT time zone and writes UTC into it.** When
`node-postgres` reads a naked timestamp it builds a `Date` **in the process's LOCAL zone** — and
this machine is **EAT (UTC+3)** — so `.toISOString()` silently subtracts three hours. `now()` is
a genuine `timestamptz` and round-trips correctly, which is what makes the pair so convincing:
**one clock in the same script is right and the other is wrong, and they disagree by exactly the
offset of the room you are sitting in.**

⛔ **THE RULE, and it extends session 24's:** that session learned *"read the instant from the
DB, the `Date` header, or a row the server wrote — never from `new Date()` on this machine."*
**That is not sufficient.** A row the server wrote, read through the driver, is ALSO local-time
poisoned. **Use `"col"::text` (this session is `Etc/UTC`, so it is already true UTC), or cast
explicitly — never the driver's `Date` for a Prisma `DateTime` column.** 📌 `s29-board-state.cjs`
uses `::text` throughout and has been telling the truth all along; `.qa-s30/round-watch.cjs`
used `.toISOString()` and was the one lying. ✅ **Verified the other way too:** the proof's
`Observed 23:56:20 EAT` matches the observation's stored `20:56:20` UTC exactly. **The
settlement proof is correct on every line.**

⭐⭐ **BUT THE REAL FINDING IS WHY A DOCUMENTED TRAP CAUGHT ANOTHER SESSION. §3's remedy pointed
at code that did not exist.** It read *"use the harness (`live/harness.mjs` sets the type parsers
for OIDs 1114/1082)"*, and **`setTypeParser` appeared nowhere in this repository** —
`harness.mjs` is a Playwright driver that never imports `pg`. So a session that did exactly what
the trap list told it to do would import the harness and then **trust `.toISOString()`**, which
is the trap wearing the remedy's clothes. ⛔ **A trap list whose remedy does not exist is worse
than no remedy at all.** Fixed by making the remedy real rather than by rewording it:
**`scripts/live/db.cjs`** sets the 1114/1082 parsers to return the raw string and carries the
`postgres.railway.internal` → public-proxy rewrite that every probe in this repo copy-pastes,
and §3 now names both working remedies. **The lesson generalises past timestamps: when a trap
recurs, check whether its documented fix is real before writing the warning a second time.**

⛔ **A SECOND THING I NEARLY FILED, AND IT WAS THE PICTURE LYING THIS TIME.** In the 700ms shot
the pool card reads `Up 100%` on the left and, at 12px, what looks like **`8% Down`** — over
`TZS 0`. A crowd bar claiming 8% on a side holding nothing would be a false money statement.
**Read as code points it is `[48,37]` — `0% Down`.** The product is right. `8` and `0` are one
pixel apart in this face, which is the same trap as `--:--` versus `—:—`: **when a digit decides
whether something is a defect, read the string, never the pixels.**

⭐ **THE ONE TO CARRY FORWARD FROM E-64: the guard caught ITSELF being vacuous, twice over.**

  **twice in one session** (`voids / resolved`, then `Math.floor(Date.now() / 1000) * 1000`), and it

  CRLF and the anchors were `\n`. The harness told the truth only because it checks its own anchors
  before believing a green — keep that check in every new harness.

  native command returns non-zero on success. Verify a build with `$LASTEXITCODE`, not by grepping.
- **PowerShell splats a comma-separated argument into separate arguments** — quote every list.

audit of session 38's close-out found exactly that, ten instruments named and none on disk.

rather than expecting to find them.** The table below is the historical scratchpad layout:

each one exists because a claim needed evidence the product could not supply about itself:

| File | Does | Why it exists |
|---|---|---|

| `payout-probe.cjs` | who owns a stuck payout, and does the ledger tie | a `DRIFT` it reported was **my instrument**, not the product: it forgot `hold`. `balance + hold` is the identity |

| `return-stuck-payout.mjs` | drives the real *Return to player* control | **dry-run by default**; snapshots the wallet before AND after and asserts the delta. ⚠️ its "blocked" check matched a word the page already contains — scope to the element |
| `da5-verify.mjs` / `da7-verify.mjs` | money-display truth on production | compare the RENDERED figure to the `Position` row. **The product cannot be its own witness about money** |
